purpose: Names that appear in search results for 'Michelin restaurants Asheville' but are NOT in the Michelin selection. Any pipeline run that emits one of these into the registry has a sourcing bug. Treat as a regression test.
trap_source: Yelp serves a page titled 'Best Michelin Restaurants in Asheville' that is an SEO listing, not the Michelin selection.

not_in_selection.name: Chai Pani
not_in_selection.note: widely covered Asheville restaurant, not in the Michelin 15

rule: An AWARD claim requires a citation to the award program or dated ceremony coverage. Aggregator and SEO pages are never sufficient in EITHER direction -- they cannot establish an award and they cannot establish its absence. REGISTRY membership is a separate and much lower bar: someone added the record and said where it came from.

corrected_entries.name: The Admiral
corrected_entries.why_it_was_wrong: Listed as not-in-selection because it appeared on a Yelp SEO page titled 'Best Michelin Restaurants in Asheville' alongside genuine non-members. The inference was that everything on an SEO page is a false positive. The Admiral is in fact on the Recommended list, confirmed by the Explore Asheville press release, WLOS, WNC Business and Visit North Carolina.
corrected_entries.lesson: An aggregator page can contain TRUE entries mixed with false ones. Appearing on a bad page is not evidence of non-membership, exactly as a non-match in the lexicon is not evidence of absence. Membership is decided by citation to the award source or dated ceremony coverage, per restaurant, in both directions.

scope: These names are NOT in the Michelin selection. That is a statement about one AWARD CLAIM, not about registry membership. Any of them may be in the guide -- several already are. This file exists to stop a false Michelin badge, nothing more.
